candidateRows.title: Python lint security patterns and formatting
candidateRows.risk: Required static checks are omitted or their effective source scope drifts
candidateRows.rationale: The existing requirement-command admission rejects a missing exact tuple. Ruff is a configured native baseline; this assertion proves binding retention, not completeness of Ruff rules or their actual input set.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Strict Python types and model construction
candidateRows.risk: Type configuration or runtime scalar admission diverges from its owner
candidateRows.rationale: Mypy configuration is present and its Python target is checked against the toolchain; runtime request-model tests reject noncanonical names and wrong scalar types. Neither is proof of arbitrary dynamic effects.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Dependency lock and installed environment identity
candidateRows.risk: Installation uses undeclared dependencies or loses hash admission
candidateRows.rationale: The native install witness assertion requires hash-checked strict synchronization and an offline no-dependency editable project install.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Python package and resource inventory
candidateRows.risk: Built distribution omits or changes requirement-owned resources
candidateRows.rationale: Package inspection rejects missing or incorrect owned-resource cardinality. Runtime import, package surface and final-container startup remain separate native witnesses.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Native domain and state-machine laws
candidateRows.risk: A legal-looking plan omits a required witness or weaker depth is accepted
candidateRows.rationale: The existing planner asserts shared witnesses take the maximum required depth. This is one concrete domain law; the full domain assertion denominator is not derived from one test.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Coverage scope and risk-owned floors
candidateRows.risk: Coverage execution silently narrows the declared backend population
candidateRows.rationale: The coverage-wrapper assertion preserves complete pytest selection and branch measurement under the declared process bound. Coverage remains an observation, not adequacy proof.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Python import authority and architectural boundaries
candidateRows.risk: Application code imports forbidden transport or runtime authority
candidateRows.rationale: Existing negative import probes reject infrastructure and maintained HTTP-client authority at the application boundary. Architecture semantic decomposition still needs its repository-owned proof.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Generated domain and state-space laws
candidateRows.risk: Selected examples fail to expose a domain counterexample
candidateRows.rationale: An existing Hypothesis-backed API generator and independently falsified response oracle cover three named operations. This is not general property coverage of planning, canonicalization, leases or all inputs.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit on a named independent law or state-machine counterexample outside the admitted generated API corpus.

candidateRows.title: Generated OpenAPI and browser type parity
candidateRows.risk: Producer and generated client contract drift
candidateRows.rationale: The native assertion changes generated bytes and requires stale-contract rejection; coverage is the declared operator API projection, not all backend routes.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on route, DTO, generator, runtime or projection-scope changes.

candidateRows.title: HTTP input and authorization boundaries
candidateRows.risk: Invalid identity, role or scope reaches an effect-capable port
candidateRows.rationale: Native controls assert unauthorized and invalid-scope requests are typed and effect-free. Full route/credential-plane closure remains a separate assertion inventory.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Reopen when any route, credential plane, request policy or port authority changes.

candidateRows.title: Schema-generated API boundary cases
candidateRows.risk: Generated requests satisfy the schema but violate request-to-port binding
candidateRows.rationale: Schemathesis/Hypothesis already exercise exactly three declared operations. The independent oracle rejects consistently corrupted scope, actor, limit or call multiplicity. This does not cover every public endpoint.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Reopen when profile.OPERATIONS, schema, harness ports, generator or independent response oracle changes.

candidateRows.title: Consumer-scoped API backward compatibility
candidateRows.risk: Published request or response semantics change without an admitted version boundary
candidateRows.rationale: CORE-010 owns immutable published domains; UI-004 parity and CONTROL-009 exact route/profile guards exist. Those assertions do not compare every released consumer against the candidate API; no whole-API backward-compatibility claim is made. A release baseline and consumer compatibility policy remain to be admitted.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit on public API/schema version changes or admission of a supported consumer baseline.

candidateRows.title: Migration lineage and packaged database schema
candidateRows.risk: Upgrade or downgrade changes retained capability lineage or destroys retained data
candidateRows.rationale: Real-PostgreSQL tests verify expand upgrade/downgrade and replay preserve the exact declaration chain. Full data-preservation and predecessor artifact rollback remain their own required witnesses.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Real transaction role and lock semantics
candidateRows.risk: Expired issuance survives a database wait or excess privileges become available
candidateRows.rationale: A real PostgreSQL lock/deadline witness rejects expired issuance and asserts no plan or audit insert. This does not exhaust every transaction or privilege combination.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Metadata-to-migration parity
candidateRows.risk: SQLAlchemy metadata changes without the corresponding migration
candidateRows.rationale: The Alembic environment supplies target_metadata and native compatibility/attestation witnesses already own live schema truth. A distinct autogenerate/check predicate requires proving incremental value and a disposable database profile; no absence of migration checks is claimed.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit on a metadata/migration divergence not rejected by current attestation or when the schema owner admits an autogenerate parity gate.

candidateRows.title: PostgreSQL SQL syntax and style
candidateRows.risk: Handwritten SQL is syntactically wrong or violates an admitted style rule
candidateRows.rationale: The bootstrap SQL includes psql-specific commands and live provisioning has a native owner. A separate SQLFluff grammar and style policy are not admitted by this candidate mapping.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when handwritten SQL expands or an independently reproducible dialect/style gap is shown.

candidateRows.title: Query and migration performance budgets
candidateRows.risk: Valid database operations exceed admitted latency, lock or capacity budgets
candidateRows.rationale: RUNTIME-036 has independent complete-metric and budget admission falsifiers. These consume synthetic signed measurements and do not measure EXPLAIN plans, query scale or migration lock duration. A representative disposable PostgreSQL performance corpus remains unqualified.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit on measured hot-query or migration-lock risk, capacity-profile changes or admission of a representative performance fixture.

candidateRows.title: Frontend lint types and unit baseline
candidateRows.risk: Promise ownership is missed by generic compilation or lint
candidateRows.rationale: The static Promise corpus verifies the exact typed rule and severity on imported React overloads, thenables and socket promises. Other Biome/type/test predicates retain their native command owners; this is not complete async-lifetime proof.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Production assets manifest and packaged UI
candidateRows.risk: Production bundle serves changed or unlisted assets
candidateRows.rationale: The existing manifest falsifier rejects changed or extra assets independently of filename shape; browser runtime and container startup are separate witnesses.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: UI state oracles and mutation sensitivity
candidateRows.risk: A late response replaces the current UI generation or a collection failure is misreported as a killed mutant
candidateRows.rationale: The current-snapshot test completes the new response before the abandoned response and requires object-identical preserved state for scope, limit, authority and refresh changes. The mutation-report falsifier distinguishes actual assertion failure from collection failure. Full mutation adequacy is not inferred.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

bindings.assertion: a late response from an abandoned %s generation preserves the current snapshot

candidateRows.title: Browser accessibility and viewport behavior
candidateRows.risk: UI controls or evidence views fail accessible navigation or layout
candidateRows.rationale: Playwright exercises the assembled UI with intercepted API fixtures and asserts no axe violations. Automated accessibility is not full WCAG or connected-backend proof.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

bindings.assertion: has no automatically detectable accessibility violations

candidateRows.title: Connected administrator journey
candidateRows.risk: Browser recovery or mutation behavior diverges across identity, API and persistence boundaries
candidateRows.rationale: The required disposable Keycloak/browser/application/PostgreSQL budget-policy witness checks a real authenticated mutation, reload, independently read persisted bytes and audit, exact replay and rejected effects. Other administrator operations and production identity integration remain separate obligations. Source binding is configured, not execution proof.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when a controlled connected administrator fixture and its environment authority are admitted.

bindings.assertion: configuration source, retained epochs and confirmed rollback at ${width}px
real administrator budget mutation has one persisted audited effect

candidateRows.title: Unused frontend files exports and dependencies
candidateRows.risk: Dynamic entrypoints are incorrectly deleted or unused code hides ownership drift
candidateRows.rationale: A reliable Knip entry graph must include generated contracts, browser, dev and build roots. No standalone unused-code contract is admitted; tool absence is not treated as a production defect.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when an owner identifies an unused-code risk and supplies complete entrypoint and dynamic-reference dispositions.

candidateRows.title: Frontend cycles and dependency rules
candidateRows.risk: A generic cycle signal is promoted to an unauthorized architecture failure
candidateRows.rationale: Repository-owned capability isolation and decomposition policy already decide forbidden co-ownership. A dependency-cruiser profile requires a unique forbidden-edge predicate and independent counterexample.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when a frontend dependency rule cannot be enforced by the current owner and a safe rule-specific corpus is available.

candidateRows.title: CSS assets and frontend performance budgets
candidateRows.risk: Valid assets are changed or missing, or rendering exceeds an unadmitted budget
candidateRows.rationale: UI-014 tests bind every served asset to the generated manifest and reject changed or extra assets. CSS static coverage and browser correctness do not establish a bundle-size or user-perceived performance budget; those operands remain owner decisions.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when UI owners admit bundle/performance limits or expose a CSS rule gap.

candidateRows.title: Standalone shell dialect analysis
candidateRows.risk: Extensionless or nested shell inputs escape lint admission
candidateRows.rationale: The repository test requires every tracked shell/shebang source to be admitted by the standalone dialect inventory; native ShellCheck is already part of workflow.lint.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Shell formatting
candidateRows.risk: An unowned formatting convention generates noise or rewrites intentional shell layout
candidateRows.rationale: Dialect-aware ShellCheck exists; a separate shfmt formatting policy and accepted authored-source corpus are not admitted by this row.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when the shell owner adopts a precise formatting convention with a check-only migration plan.

candidateRows.title: Workflow syntax expressions and fixture closure
candidateRows.risk: Distributed or fixture workflows are missing from syntax analysis
candidateRows.rationale: Native workflow wrapper tests reject incomplete and nonregular workflow/shell inputs and preserve the locked actionlint/zizmor closure.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Workflow security and immutable control dependencies
candidateRows.risk: Workflow analysis loses its pinned analyzer or least-privilege control scope
candidateRows.rationale: Existing tests require exact linters in the provider quality gate. Offline analyzer success does not establish transitive action download safety or every provider security property.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Strict JSON syntax and ambiguous-value rejection
candidateRows.risk: Duplicate keys or nonfinite values yield ambiguous configuration
candidateRows.rationale: Native JSON admission has negative ambiguous-value cases under the existing quality owner; domain schema predicates remain separate.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: YAML syntax and duplicate-key admission
candidateRows.risk: Configuration files are omitted or interpreted under an unintended YAML contract
candidateRows.rationale: The utility selects hidden and nested YAML and invokes the strict pinned parser. The selected assertion proves command/input selection; effective parser coverage is a separate correction concern and not inferred from suffix membership.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when YAML source roots, dialect, anchors, parser rules or effective-input policy change.

candidateRows.title: Version-bound vendor schema validation
candidateRows.risk: Untrusted or stale schema references change the admitted input language
candidateRows.rationale: Pinned offline bundles and local reference checks are present. The selected negative assertion independently rejects changed provenance and remote references; this covers admitted schema families, not every vendor schema.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify when a vendor schema, dialect, reference closure or configuration family changes.

candidateRows.title: TOML parse and manifest coherence
candidateRows.risk: TOML files are parseable but disagree with locked toolchain identity
candidateRows.rationale: The toolchain-owner assertion parses authored mise configuration and lock data and enforces exact versions/platform identities. Arbitrary new TOML roots are not thereby proved consumed.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Authored TOML formatting
candidateRows.risk: Formatter policy is applied to generated lock data without an owner
candidateRows.rationale: Syntax and toolchain coherence have native owners. A separate Taplo formatting policy needs an authored-file scope and incremental benefit; generated locks are excluded from manual formatting.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when an authored TOML formatting policy is adopted; preserve native lock bytes.

candidateRows.title: Task DAG and toolchain pin parity
candidateRows.risk: A second task facade changes commands or versions silently
candidateRows.rationale: The exact mise/lock assertion verifies installation and task projections, required dependency edges and supported platform sets.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Docker build checks
candidateRows.risk: A Dockerfile is missed or native build-check warnings do not fail
candidateRows.rationale: The native wrapper test requires all Dockerfile naming forms, the fixed builder and error=true. Builder execution/metadata/network behavior requires its actual provider run.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when Dockerfile inventory, context, frontend, builder or BuildKit output contract changes.

candidateRows.title: Docker RUN and package lint
candidateRows.risk: A scoped exception suppresses an unrelated Dockerfile finding
candidateRows.rationale: Hadolint is already configured and its source-bound exception falsifier rejects changed source and unrelated warnings. Whole rule adequacy and actual execution remain distinct.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when Dockerfiles, Hadolint rules, version or exception bytes change.

candidateRows.title: Build context and final image runtime
candidateRows.risk: Build assets or dependency artifacts differ from intended production inputs
candidateRows.rationale: Frontend manifest tests independently reject nonproduction evidence; runtime container witnesses retain their separate provider authority. Docker context closure is not inferred from this asset assertion.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Compose configuration resolution
candidateRows.risk: Malformed Compose/provider configuration reaches mutation
candidateRows.rationale: The native Compose test rejects unsupported or malformed Compose before mutation; early offline schema checks supplement it and do not establish successful startup.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Connected development stack lifecycle
candidateRows.risk: Failed admission or shutdown is crossed by later provider mutations
candidateRows.rationale: Native lifecycle tests require up to stop at failed admission/runtime boundaries. Real stack health, roles, watch and cleanup still require their explicit service witnesses.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Devcontainer host and runtime boundary
candidateRows.risk: Devcontainer configuration gains host Docker authority or unpinned tool state
candidateRows.rationale: The existing configuration assertion forbids host Docker authority and pins dependencies. This source witness is distinct from the provider-backed devcontainer verification.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Markdown graph links and authority roots
candidateRows.risk: Documents or local links escape the rooted authority graph
candidateRows.rationale: The native graph falsifier rejects unreachable Markdown; other graph tests retain strict URL, symlink, UTF-8 and resource boundaries.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Markdown style
candidateRows.risk: Style findings become an unauthorized semantic or historical-document rewrite
candidateRows.rationale: Documentation graph, diagrams and spelling are existing independent owners. A Markdown formatting/style subset requires an owner-approved policy and historical/generated exclusions.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when a concrete readability/style rule is adopted with a source-preserving remediation path.

candidateRows.title: Public external link availability
candidateRows.risk: Temporary network errors are mistaken for permanently broken authoritative references
candidateRows.rationale: The documentation owner syntax-admits external HTTPS links without fetching in the deterministic gate. A scheduled reachability lane requires bounded egress and a retry/unknown policy.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when external-link freshness is owner-required and scheduled egress plus non-actionable failure handling are admitted.

candidateRows.title: Prometheus rules and alert semantics
candidateRows.risk: Rule syntax or alert fixtures drift from the admitted Prometheus runtime
candidateRows.rationale: The wrapper test binds immutable promtool, read-only inputs and no network. Expected-alert semantics require the native promtool fixture execution; YAML validity is not a substitute.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Requirement documentation runtime and config coherence
candidateRows.risk: Version projection drift is hidden by coincidental text equality
candidateRows.rationale: Native toolchain tests distinguish Python minor-target projection from exact patch pins. This is a named-value relation and does not grep historical prose into one version.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Path mode symlink and generated-source admission
candidateRows.risk: Input identity or file kind changes without renewed admission
candidateRows.rationale: Native input falsifiers reject leaf/parent symlinks, missing files, directories and binary data. The 8e50b717 review epoch still leaves the separate early mode-change fallback concern for the correction batch; this row does not declare that correction proven.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when index path/mode identity, source roots, generated provenance or effective-input admission changes.

candidateRows.title: Python and Node dependency vulnerabilities
candidateRows.risk: One supported runtime or dependency lock is absent from the advisory scan
candidateRows.rationale: The native command assertion covers supported Python versions and the frontend lock. Fresh-on-execution is not a periodic deployed-artifact requalification claim.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when supported runtime/platform/package scopes, feed contracts or freshness cadence change.

candidateRows.title: New dependency risk review
candidateRows.risk: PR dependency changes bypass their immutable provider action
candidateRows.rationale: The tracked workflow assertion binds dependency-review to its immutable action. Entitlement, provider graph completeness and live run evidence were not read in this lane.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Provider CodeQL security analysis
candidateRows.risk: Configured provider security analysis is mistaken for current complete results
candidateRows.rationale: The matrix delegates this check to provider-owned default setup. No source test can establish its current languages, query suite, trigger outcomes or alert completeness.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit using an exact provider configuration and analysis snapshot bound to source/run/query identities.

candidateRows.title: Secret detection in source and history
candidateRows.risk: Provider or offline scanning is assumed to cover unobserved patterns and history
candidateRows.rationale: The matrix names provider secret scanning and push protection. This read-only source lane does not requalify provider pattern/history coverage or an offline custom-rule delta. Scanner absence is not an absence-of-checks claim.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit with authorized provider evidence and a same-corpus assessment of any proposed offline incremental scope.

candidateRows.title: Delivered image vulnerability admission
candidateRows.risk: A fresh scan belongs to another image or silently suppresses actionable vulnerabilities
candidateRows.rationale: The existing release owner binds image/index/child/platform, pinned scanner and database, and rejects effective caller suppressions. Covered means the named admission predicate has configured negative assertions; release execution and unknown-vulnerability absence are not claimed. Periodic rechecks discover the latest successful release, bind its immutable image to verified source and run certificates, and reuse the current image vulnerability policy. This does not inventory every deployed or retained historical image.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify scanner, database schema, distro, platform, image relation or suppression defaults.

candidateRows.title: SBOM provenance and release identity
candidateRows.risk: Foreign or structurally vacuous attestations are accepted as release evidence
candidateRows.rationale: Native predicate admission rejects invalid provenance dimensions and non-meaningful SPDX package evidence. Source assertions are executed by Full Check; real attestations remain owned by the separate release workflow.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit on signer, workflow, subject, predicate schema or release generation changes.

candidateRows.title: Additional artifact inventory
candidateRows.risk: A second SBOM or scanner duplicates the admitted release baseline without new evidence
candidateRows.rationale: The release owner already supplies BuildKit SPDX and Grype. Additional Syft/inventory diversity requires a concrete omitted package/source predicate; schema validity does not prove inventory completeness.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when release package evidence exposes a specific inventory gap or independent inventory requirement.

candidateRows.title: Custom forbidden API and trust patterns
candidateRows.risk: Generic SAST duplicates current rules or loses a repository-specific boundary
candidateRows.rationale: Repository-owned import gates and provider CodeQL already supply distinct predicates. A Semgrep rulepack needs a named uncovered pattern and independent positive/negative corpus.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit upon a concrete rule-level gap in existing static or native witnesses.

candidateRows.title: Additional dependency ecosystem coverage
candidateRows.risk: The owned Go helper dependency universe is omitted or build-selected files are lost
candidateRows.rationale: Go vet, Staticcheck and govulncheck are already configured for each owned Go module and test sources. The frozen baseline still contains the separately reviewed cgo effective-input admission gap; correction evidence must be rebound. Native Go source discovery now rejects cgo and excluded or mismatched source cohorts before each analyzer; native import variants have a separate GitHub witness.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit on Go modules, build constraints, cgo, platforms, advisory inputs or the current admission correction.

candidateRows.title: Dependency and source license obligations
candidateRows.risk: A structurally valid SBOM is mistaken for license approval
candidateRows.rationale: Release SBOM requirements validate structure and provenance. The finite admitted requirement sources do not establish a license allow/deny policy or an authorized legal decision owner; no legal permissibility is inferred. Selecting ScanCode cannot supply that missing policy.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when an authorized owner admits license obligations, unknown-license disposition and the dependency/source distribution scope.

candidateRows.title: External artifact signature and provenance verification
candidateRows.risk: Valid attestations belong to a foreign signer workflow or image
candidateRows.rationale: The existing release verifier architecture uses a no-checkout job and never executes the image. Exact provider verification requires the separate release run and is not replaced by local structural assertions.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on changes to the named owner, assertion, source scope, command or dependency epoch.

candidateRows.title: Vulnerability exceptions and triage
candidateRows.risk: A suppression or VEX statement erases an unresolved vulnerability
candidateRows.rationale: Current release policy intentionally rejects caller VEX/ignore/exclusion suppressions. A positive waiver lifecycle is not admitted; adding one requires a separate owner decision and exact artifact/rule/expiry binding. The separate scheduled advisory workflow rechecks unchanged lock and released-image subjects; receipt acceptance binds source, every required scope and a 36-hour maximum observation age. Missed scheduler execution and notification subscriptions remain operational obligations.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit only when the release owner admits a concrete exception workflow; retain unsuppressed raw verdicts meanwhile.

candidateRows.title: CDK cloud assembly completeness
candidateRows.risk: Missing stage, stack or asset in a synthesized cloud assembly
candidateRows.rationale: The admitted product/build surface owns a Python service, React UI, OCI images and Compose development resources; AWS CDK cloud-assembly synthesis is not an adopted coordinator capability. This disposition is specific to CDK assembly, not generic build correctness.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: An admitted CDK stage/stack/asset assembly or infrastructure source root is added.

candidateRows.title: CloudFormation security and resource schemas
candidateRows.risk: Valid infrastructure syntax hides forbidden IAM or network authority
candidateRows.rationale: The frozen coordinator capability and build inventory has no adopted CloudFormation/CDK deployment contract. Docker, GitHub and runtime authorization remain separately applicable.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: A repository-owned synthesized CloudFormation or AWS policy surface is adopted.

candidateRows.title: Proxy public configuration and secret precedence
candidateRows.risk: Runtime or browser configuration exposes secrets or bypasses authentication
candidateRows.rationale: Native development image assertions require owner-only secret files to be copied into private tmpfs and constrain runtime identity. This does not prove a deployment proxy or protected-stage end-to-end configuration.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: Deployment source generation and cleanup
candidateRows.risk: A workflow publishes or verifies a foreign source/image generation
candidateRows.rationale: Release assertions bind exact source and registry digest; deployment rollout, startup and rollback are separate environment-specific witnesses and are not inferred from build success.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: Observability units dimensions and redaction
candidateRows.risk: Telemetry labels or missing data misrepresent authority or leak sensitive values
candidateRows.rationale: Prometheus has a pinned native rule/test command. CloudWatch/OTel-specific dimensions are not inherited; exact runtime telemetry and redaction retain their current owners.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: Anonymized restore disposition
candidateRows.risk: A restored dataset exposes PII or breaks foreign-key closure
candidateRows.rationale: The admitted database lifecycle owns coordinator evidence and migrations; it does not admit a production-data anonymization/restore transformation. Migration retention requirements remain applicable under DB01/CI13.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: A database-copy or anonymization product/operations capability is admitted.

candidateRows.title: Backup restore and cutover fidelity
candidateRows.risk: A backup restore drops retained evidence or publishes a partial database
candidateRows.rationale: Migration rollback/retention is admitted, but it does not itself prove backup restore or an operational recovery-point/time contract. This bounded lane has no environment-bound restore evidence and does not claim the operation is absent.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when the persistence/operations owner identifies the supported backup/restore procedure and exact recovery/cutover witnesses.

candidateRows.title: Database dialect and principal-specific semantics
candidateRows.risk: A database surrogate or different dialect is mistaken for PostgreSQL authority
candidateRows.rationale: The coordinator owns PostgreSQL and real privilege tests reject PUBLIC/schema/append-only violations. Other consumers SQL Server/Oracle/Fabric/BigQuery clauses are outside the adopted backend runtime.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: Read-only data and scope authorization
candidateRows.risk: A read operation changes actor, repository, cursor or query scope
candidateRows.rationale: The request oracle rejects a consistently changed port and response scope. This is a fixed repository-query contract, not admission of arbitrary untrusted SQL or generic query rewriting.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: CSV and spreadsheet data conversion
candidateRows.risk: Tabular import/export changes decimals, dates, encoding or inert text
candidateRows.rationale: The current finite versioned API/configuration contracts exchange strict JSON and retained JSON/YAML source, not CSV/XLSX conversion. This disposition is scoped to tabular conversion, not all exports.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: A CSV/XLSX import/export operation or spreadsheet artifact is admitted.

candidateRows.title: Report source lineage and trust
candidateRows.risk: Provider-only or uploaded facts acquire an unsupported provenance class
candidateRows.rationale: The measurement falsifier rejects provider-only facts masquerading as webhook evidence. Complete source/report-pointer lifecycle coverage requires its own relation and retention assertions.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: Batch provenance and generation accounting
candidateRows.risk: Retry or partial ingestion changes business keys or falsely advances freshness
candidateRows.rationale: Current archive requirements RUNTIME-046 through RUNTIME-055 own generation, keys, quotas and progress. This candidate spans several independently owned ingestion relations; one batch-function name or generic DB test cannot close it. The lane has not completed their assertion partition.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit with an explicit partition of archive batch, generation, source-key and retry assertions under their existing requirements.

candidateRows.title: Archive and binary input materialization
candidateRows.risk: Encoded archives expand beyond resource limits or escape the output root
candidateRows.rationale: Current bounded source/report and package readers have distinct owners. The specialized ZIP/MIME/MSG/OOXML decompression surface is not established or disproved by the tool inventory; no archive-safety coverage is inferred from JSON bounds.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit when a concrete archive producer/consumer and its decode/materialization boundary are identified.

candidateRows.title: Document rendering and OCR semantics
candidateRows.risk: PDF/OCR/image/slide conversion loses visible content or geometry
candidateRows.rationale: The coordinator owns web assets and documentation diagrams, not an admitted document-conversion or OCR pipeline. Diagram and frontend asset contracts are accounted separately.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: A PDF/OCR/image/slide ingestion or transformation capability is adopted.

candidateRows.title: XML SOAP and invoice wire conformance
candidateRows.risk: Namespaces, encodings or financial sums violate an XML consumer contract
candidateRows.rationale: The admitted public transport surface is JSON/HTTP with exact generated contracts; it has no SOAP/XML invoice conformance capability. JSON wire tests are not substituted for XML proof.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: An XML/SOAP or electronic-invoice consumer contract is adopted.

candidateRows.title: Executable agent tool authorization
candidateRows.risk: An agent tool call expands approval, tenant or effect authority
candidateRows.rationale: The adopted agent capability supplies bounded risk advice and may not name execution authority. It is not an executable agent tool registry. Advice monotonicity is independently applicable under CI05.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: An executable tool registry or agent-driven provider write is admitted.

candidateRows.title: Durable agent sessions and checkpoints
candidateRows.risk: Agent memory replay or checkpoint recovery changes conversation state
candidateRows.rationale: Coordinator policy/audit persistence does not create an agent conversation, WAL or memory-session capability. General durable-state requirements are separately applicable under CI12-CI16.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Durable agent sessions, checkpoints or memory replay enter the product contract.

candidateRows.title: SSE WebSocket and NDJSON stream protocol
candidateRows.risk: Streaming chunks violate framing, cancellation or conversation scope
candidateRows.rationale: The admitted product API/UI contract does not define an SSE/WebSocket/NDJSON conversation protocol. HTTP body bounds and development-server sockets do not establish that product surface.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: A product streaming protocol or reconnect contract is added.

candidateRows.title: Retrieval corpus ACL and citation lineage
candidateRows.risk: Search returns another tenant corpus or unsupported citations
candidateRows.rationale: The product evidence queries are bounded authoritative repository projections; no retrieval/vector corpus or citation-quality subsystem is adopted. SQL read authorization remains independently applicable.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: A retrieval corpus, search index with tenant ACL, or generated citation capability is adopted.

candidateRows.title: Model quality and independent evaluation
candidateRows.risk: Advice without accepted independent evaluation is mistaken for trustworthy guidance
candidateRows.rationale: Risk-advice admission rejects otherwise valid advice when its independent evaluation fails. This proves an admission predicate, not held-out model quality, calibration, grounding or cost performance.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: Audio and speech lifecycle
candidateRows.risk: Cancelled audio is applied to another conversation or media resources leak
candidateRows.rationale: No voice recording/transcription/STT operation exists in the admitted finite product API and browser capability contracts.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: An audio/media capture, transcription or STT provider boundary is adopted.

candidateRows.title: Background work retry lease and recovery
candidateRows.risk: Background work redelivery repeats an effect or falsely records progress
candidateRows.rationale: The coordinator has native PostgreSQL-backed collection/reconciliation lanes, not the blueprint consumers Celery stack. Existing RUNTIME-048/054 lifecycle owners apply; the complete scheduler/lease/crash assertion partition remains unresolved in this bounded mapping.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Revisit with lane-specific acknowledgement, lease, idempotency, crash and shutdown witnesses rather than adding a broker plugin by name.

candidateRows.title: Offline client write replay
candidateRows.risk: Offline queued writes cross identity or replay in the wrong order
candidateRows.rationale: The current operator UI is an online projection with explicit unavailable/unknown outcomes; no service-worker/IndexedDB/native offline-write queue is admitted. Retry of one retained operation is covered by the existing online command contract.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: An offline write queue, service worker or native bridge gains product authority.

candidateRows.title: Web composition and mounted assets

candidateRows.rationale: The production asset manifest has a native mutation falsifier binding exact bytes independent of filenames. Jinja and embedded report host-specific clauses activate only with such a consumer.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.title: Time filters ordering and pagination semantics
candidateRows.risk: A response looks coherent after the request cursor or filter was changed
candidateRows.rationale: The status oracle independently rejects cursor substitution even when returned rows are unchanged. Locale/DST and every analytics pagination contract require separate owner-specific assertions.
candidateRows.revisitWhen: Requalify on any change to the named owner, requirement, source scope, assertion or command.

candidateRows.revisitWhen: A geospatial planning or physical routing domain becomes an adopted capability.
